# Archival Dispatch: 10 Master Broadcasts Dated Across Phil Rizzuto Bill Stern, Glenn Miller, and WWII Sugar Rationing

**Date**: 2026-08-21  
**Author**: radio index  
**Tags**: Phil Rizzuto, Bill Stern, Sports Caravan, Tom Duggan, Tug Wilson, Big Ten, WWII Home Front, War Production Board, Sugar Rationing, War Bonds, GI Jill, AFRS, Glenn Miller, Chesterfield Moonlight Serenade, Franz Boas, Lest We Forget, Parry O'Brien, Greatest Sports Thrills, Andy Russell, Guest Star, David Rose, Original Filenames

---

## Batch 97 Forensic Discoveries

Batch 97 recovers and dates 10 significant historical recordings spanning mid-century sports broadcasting, WWII wartime home front civil mobilization, big band radio sponsorships, civil rights and cultural anthropology, Olympic athletics, and pop vocal standards: New York Yankees Hall of Fame shortstop Phil Rizzuto interviewing legendary NBC sportscaster Bill Stern on ***Phil Rizzuto's Sports Caravan*** (1953), Chicago commentator Tom Duggan interviewing Big Ten Commissioner and Olympic Committee president Kenneth 'Tug' Wilson (1952), 3 rare WWII radio spots including the War Production Board's official Sugar Rationing broadcast guide (1942), the US Treasury's Second War Loan Drive campaign (1943), and GI Jill urging servicemen to invest in war bonds on AFRS (1944), Glenn Miller and His Orchestra broadcasting their signature *Moonlight Serenade* for Chesterfield cigarettes (1940), an educational radio dramatization celebrating the life and anti-racism research of anthropologist Franz Boas on ***Lest We Forget*** (1948), Olympic shot put champion Parry O'Brien recounting his world record on ***Greatest Sports Thrills*** (1955), Latin-pop singer Andy Russell backed by Harry Sosnik on the US Treasury's ***Guest Star*** (1949), and David Rose and His Orchestra (1950).
